title: How is the sum of three dates in a row linked to the middle date?
description: A row of three dates is taken from the calendar, with the middle date called a. The left date is one less and the right date is one more, and adding all three leaves a multiple of the middle date. Keeko's doubt is that the sum is the middle date plus two.
teaching_notes: One idea: the plus one and minus one cancel, so three copies of the middle date are left. Watch for students who count the middle date only once.

source: Find another shape on the calendar whose sum is a multiple o
video_script.why: A learner finds another calendar shape whose sum is a multiple of one of its dates, using the middle date a.
video_script.substitution: a row of three calendar dates with the middle date a, checked on fourteen, fifteen and sixteen
video_script.anchor: a row of three calendar dates with a in the middle
video_script.wrong_answer: the sum is the middle date plus two
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the middle date only once and keeps a plus two. For fourteen, fifteen and sixteen that gives seventeen, but the dates add to forty five, because the middle date is counted in all three dates.
video_script.payoff_line: The sum of three dates in a row is three eigh

final_answer.value: 3a for a row of three dates with middle a ; 45 for 14, 15, 16
final_answer.spoken: three eigh for a row with middle date eigh, and forty five for fourteen, fifteen and sixteen

maths_rules: the row is a - 1, a, a + 1
a column of three dates is a - 7, a, a + 7 and its sum is 3a + (-7 + 7) = 3a
video_script.design: One row of three dates stays on the board. The left and right dates are written with a, the three are added, and the plus one and minus one are cancelled.

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Step one, write the row. The left date is eigh minus one, and the middle date is eigh. The right date is eigh plus one.

marks.group: the three a's and the plain numbers are grouped
marks.cancel: minus one and plus one cancel to give 3a

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the three dates. Terms can be added in any order, so the brackets can be opened.
<bookmark mark='group'/>There are three eighs, and the plain numbers are minus one and plus one.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>Minus one and plus one cancel to zero, so only three eighs are left.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Step three, check with the row fourteen, fifteen and sixteen. They add to forty five.
<bookmark mark='cmp'/>Three times the middle date, fifteen, is also forty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: a column of three dates a − 7, a, a + 7 also gives 3a

marks.col: a column of three dates is written beside the row

narration: <bookmark mark='col'/>Step four, try a column of three dates. The dates are eigh minus seven, eigh, and eigh plus seven.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Minus seven and plus seven cancel, so this sum is also three eigh.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3a for a row of three dates with middle a ; 45 for 14, 15, 16
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum of three dates in a row is three eigh, three times the middle date. For fourteen, fifteen and sixteen it is forty five.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the sum is the middle date plus two.
<bookmark mark='test'/>For fourteen, fifteen and sixteen, fifteen plus two is only seventeen. The three dates add to forty five.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Eigh is in all three dates, so we count it three times.
